claims.text: Ambient-temperature LPBF with conventional scanning produces equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi components that exhibit shrinkage and warping.
Ambient-temperature LPBF with conventional scanning produces equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi components containing internal voids and residual stresses.
Substrate preheating to approximately 500 °C lowers thermal gradients during LPBF of CoCrFeMnNi.
Lower thermal gradients diminish residual stresses in LPBF-built CoCrFeMnNi.
Substrate preheating slows the rapid solidification associated with LPBF.
Rapid solidification can contribute to fabrication-induced defects in LPBF CoCrFeMnNi.
A scanning strategy using longer melt-pool overlaps and reduced scan-speed variation promotes more uniform melting and solidification.
Combining 500 °C substrate preheating with the proposed scanning strategy reduces fabrication-induced defects.
The combined intervention produces a more uniform and refined microstructure.
The combined intervention reduces residual thermal stress and porosity.
The combined intervention reduces shrinkage and warping relative to ambient-temperature LPBF with conventional scanning.
The combined intervention lowers internal porosity relative to ambient-temperature LPBF with conventional scanning.
The combined intervention increases tensile strength relative to ambient-temperature LPBF with conventional scanning.
The combined intervention increases ductility relative to ambient-temperature LPBF with conventional scanning.
Excessive preheating or an unsuitable parameter balance may cause adverse grain coarsening.
